Kirara Hoshi (星 綺羅羅, *Hoshi Kirara*) is a third-year student at Tokyo Jujutsu High suspended for clashing with authority. While away from the school, Kirara has partnered with Hakari while running his fight club. Their Cursed Technique is Love Rendezvous (星間飛行, *Rabu Randebū*), a complex technique whose motif is based on the Southern Cross constellation. For someone marked with one star to approach someone marked with another star, they must follow a determined order, or else targets of the same star will attract each other. The order follows the stars from nearest to furthest distance to the Earth: Imai, Acrux, Mimosa, Ginan, and Gacrux. They agree to Megumi and Yuji's request for help, after hearing about everything that transpired at Shibuya and after. Kirara is later outside the barriers of the Culling Game serving as the provider of intel for one group.

It is set in the mid-22nd century, when humans are colonizing [Pandora](/wiki/Pandora_(Avatar) "Pandora (Avatar)"), a lush [habitable moon](/wiki/Habitable_moon "Habitable moon"), in order to mine the valuable mineral [unobtanium](/wiki/Unobtainium "Unobtainium").[[d]](#cite_note-14) The expansion of the mining colony threatens the existence of a local tribe of [Na'vi](/wiki/Fictional_universe_of_Avatar#Na'vi "Fictional universe of Avatar"), a [humanoid](/wiki/Humanoid "Humanoid") species indigenous to Pandora. The title of the film refers to an "avatar", which is a [genetically engineered](/wiki/Genetic_engineering "Genetic engineering") Na'vi body remotely operated from the brain of a human, and which is used to [interact](/wiki/Telepresence "Telepresence") with the Na'vi.

Development of *Avatar* began in 1994, when Cameron wrote an 80-page treatment for the film. Filming was due to take place after the completion of Cameron's 1997 film *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")*, for a planned release in 1999; however, according to Cameron, the necessary technology was not yet available to achieve his vision of the film. The **San Francisco 49ers** (also written as the **San Francisco Forty-Niners** and nicknamed the **Niners**)[[6]](#cite_note-7) are a professional [American football](/wiki/American_football "American football") team based in the [San Francisco Bay Area](/wiki/San_Francisco_Bay_Area "San Francisco Bay Area"). The 49ers compete in the [National Football League](/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL) as a member of the [National Football Conference](/wiki/National_Football_Conference "National Football Conference") (NFC) [West](/wiki/NFC_West "NFC West") division. The team plays its home games at [Levi's Stadium](/wiki/Levi%27s_Stadium "Levi's Stadium") in [Santa Clara, California](/wiki/Santa_Clara,_California "Santa Clara, California"), located 38 miles (61 km) southeast of [San Francisco](/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"). The team is named after the prospectors of the [California gold rush](/wiki/California_gold_rush "California gold rush").[[7]](#cite_note-8)

Main article: [History of ExxonMobil](/wiki/History_of_ExxonMobil "History of ExxonMobil")

Originally, [Vacuum Oil Company](/wiki/Vacuum_Oil_Company "Vacuum Oil Company") was founded in 1866. Vacuum Oil later was acquired by [Standard Oil](/wiki/Standard_Oil "Standard Oil") in 1879, divested from Standard in 1911 with [its legally-mandated breakup](/wiki/Standard_Oil_Co._of_New_Jersey_v._United_States "Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States"), and merged by the Standard Oil Company of New York (Socony), later known as [Mobil](/wiki/Mobil "Mobil"), in 1931. After the 1911 breakup, Standard Oil continued to exist through its New Jersey subsidiary (Jersey Standard), and retained its name in much of the eastern United States. Jersey Standard grew by acquiring [Humble Oil](/wiki/Humble_Oil "Humble Oil") in the 1930s and became the dominant oil company on the world stage.

The company's lack of ownership over the Standard Oil name across the United States, however, prompted a name change to unify all of its brands under one name, choosing Exxon in 1972 instead of continuing to use the three distinct brands [Esso](/wiki/Esso "Esso"), [Enco](/wiki/Enco_(brand) "Enco (brand)"), and [Humble Oil](/wiki/Humble_Oil "Humble Oil").[[16]](#cite_note-17)[[17]](#cite_note-Kumar_2019_101–109-18)

In 1998, the two companies agreed to merge and form ExxonMobil, with the deal closing on November 30, 1999. The new company's name containing both of the trade names of its immediate predecessors. However, the structure of the merger provided that Exxon was the surviving company and bought Mobil, rather than a new company being created.[[17]](#cite_note-Kumar_2019_101–109-18)[[18]](#cite_note-19)[[19]](#cite_note-20)[[20]](#cite_note-21) Following the merger, Exxon's NYSE ticker symbol was changed from "XON"[[21]](#cite_note-22) to "XOM".
